newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo targets 6-7 pct global mkt share for Remeron.
newsitem.headline: Akzo targets 6-7 pct global mkt share for Remeron.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel said on Thursday it was targeting a five percent share of the U.S. market for its new anti-depressant Remeron in the next couple of years and a 6-7 percent global market share within three years.
"Our sales target is five percent of the U.S. market in the coming years," finance director Jean den Hoed told a results news conference.
"Outside the U.S. this should be higher," he said, targeting a 6-7 percent share of the world market in anti-depressants in the next two to three years.
The size of the global market is estimated at some 10-11 billion guilders a year, he said.
Den Hoed said monthly U.S. sales of Remeron had more than doubled in the first half, from 3.7 million guilders in January to eight million guilders in June.
The drug, launched late last year, already commanded a U.S. market share of more than one percent, he added.
Global Remeron sales amounted to some 14 million guilders in June, or roughly 170 million guilders annually, he said.
Remeron's contribution to profits in 1997 would be limited by start-up costs, but from 1998 it would start to contribute fully, Den Hoed added.
Akzo will triple its Remeron sales force in the U.S. from 150 to 450 in the second half and the drug is due to be introduced in France at the beginning of next year.
